highlights:
## Croatia injuries ahead of World Cup
[...]
Croatia will have received a scare ahead of the World Cup when legendary midfielder Modric suffered multiple facial fractures in a clash of heads in late April while playing for his club AC Milan, but the 40-year-old will recover in time to play his usual steadfast role at the World Cup.
[...]
The only player who has missed out on a potential spot on the World Cup roster is Hajduk Split goalkeeper Ivica Ivusic, who has six international caps but lost his starting spot at the club level thanks to a four-month absence for a groin injury through the heart of the campaign and was therefore not called up.
[...]
Otherwise, all key players are fit for action, including Man City teammates Josko Gvardiol and Kovacic who both missed most of the season due to injury but recovered to play a part in the final few matches and earn spots on the World Cup roster.

results.title: Dalić: I'm very pleased with how we trained
highlights:
The Croatian national football team has completed its final training session during the Rijeka preparations. The Firebirds still have to play a Sunday friendly match against Slovenia in Varaždin before heading to the World Cup, and coach Zlatko Dalić is satisfied with what has been done.
[...]
"The last training session has been completed, the first cycle ends tomorrow. I am very pleased with how we trained. The result against Belgium was not good and that disturbed us a bit. We wanted to give everyone minutes, we wanted to get three players back into shape through the game, Kovačić, Modrić and Guardiola. There is no drama, France and the Netherlands also lost. Everyone is making ten substitutions, this is the last chance to try all the players. Everything is great. We will go 4-2-3-1, we are changing the system. Overall, I am pleased," said Dalić, referring to the change in system.
[...]
"We're getting the players back into rhythm, they're working well and that's important. We want to get them back in shape, but if they're not at the peak of their abilities, we have alternatives. Vušković is fair, he's working well, he's top in training. He has a guard in him so that the pressure doesn't eat him," added Dalić, announcing tomorrow's match against Slovenia.
[...]
"A match that gives us a chance to try new things. We're looking at the matches against Ghana and Panama to see if we'll play different systems there, and we're looking at the match against Slovenia as a good motivation for us. The Slovenians will try to cause us problems, we'll try to be real."
[...]
Journalists also asked Dalić about the positions of Luka and Petar Sučić and whether Toni Fruk would get playing time.
[...]
"Sučić was paired with Luka and it worked well. Against Belgium, we pushed him alongside Baturina because they are younger and more agile. Petar is a versatile player, he is only growing and is good. Luka Sučić has a great left foot, he is technically phenomenal. He has a place in the national team, we put him on the left flank, we need to improve his defense, but he is always ready and works well," said Dalić, adding that Toni Fruk "even though he had bad luck with his hand injury, he is unquestionable and will get his minutes."

## Tight-knit Croatia squad prepared for another lengthy World Cup run
[...]
ALEXANDRIA, Va. — Thomas Tuchel’s England World Cup squad selections caught much of the footballing world off guard.
[...]
That included Croatia defender Kristijan Jakic.
[...]
Asked on Wednesday to size up his team’s first Group L opponent after Croatia arrived at its World Cup base camp in the Washington suburbs, the 29-year-old FC Augsburg defender admitted he was among those who expected to see the likes of Phil Foden, Cole Palmer, Harry Maguire and Trent Alexander-Arnold in Tuchel’s group.
[...]
“I was surprised by their final squad list because they were missing some players that maybe you would expect,” Jakic said in Croatian. “But that also says a lot about their quality.”
[...]
While much of Croatia’s success owes to generational talents such as Luka Modric, Ivan Perisic and Mateo Kovacic, the ethos of selflessness and sacrifice Dalic appears to have instilled adds another dimension.
[...]
This is a Croatian side that will need more help from its supporting cast than previous iterations, even if the aging core of its golden generation is still present, led by the 40-year-old Modric.
[...]
This is particularly true at center forward, where it’s still unclear whether Igor Matanovic, Petar Musa or Ante Budimir will get the majority of the minutes.
[...]
“I’m not coming here with any particular expectations,” said the 23-year-old Matanovic, another Bundesliga player who scored 11 league goals for Freiburg this season. “I had a really good season in my club. But whoever plays, Budimir, Musa or myself, we are all ready.”
